items.title: Here's who is attending the Trump-Xi state dinner
items.summary: U.S. government officials, business leaders and their spouses dominated a list of more than 100 people who will attend a state dinner Thursday, according to a White House press release.

items.title: Philadelphia Fed's Anna Paulson says 'modest' rate moves likely ahead to tame inflation
items.summary: Philadelphia Federal Reserve President Anna Paulson said Thursday that she and her colleagues may need to raise interest rates further to bring inflation back to target.

items.title: China confirms first AI talks with U.S. have taken place, hints at trade truce extension
items.summary: BEIJING—China's Commerce Ministry confirmed Thursday that its senior trade negotiators had held their first talks with the U.S. on artificial intelligence.

items.title: U.S.-China trade truce extended for two months, Bessent says, as Xi begins state visit
items.summary: The U.S. and China have extended a truce to keep tariffs lower for longer and rare earths flowing, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday local time.

items.title: Trump-Xi meeting: Why China's self-sufficiency changes the calculus
items.summary: BEIJING — The trade deficit that escalated tensions between China and the U.S. in recent years has yet to shrink significantly, and the world's second-largest economy faces deep challenges.

items.title: Here's who we know is going to the Trump-Xi dinner so far
items.summary: BEIJING — With two days to go before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to land in the U.S., very little is known about which, if any, Chinese executives will join him.

items.title: Surging Treasury yields pose a brand new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
items.summary: The bond market is yelling at the Federal Reserve, but the messages are coming from different directions and pose a dilemma for policymakers as they seek to strike a balance that won't tank the economy.

items.title: Global debt tops $365 trillion as economists sound alarm over 'vicious cycle'
items.summary: Ever-higher costs to service mounting debt loads pose a major risk to governments around the world, economists have warned.

items.title: Switzerland is keeping rates at 0% — for now
items.summary: Switzerland's central bank kept its key interest rate at 0% on Thursday, defying the tightening cycle that has begun among many of its major peers.

items.title: France's fresh budget battle threatens to topple another government
items.summary: France is paying an ever-higher risk premium on its debt as investors brace for a third straight year of drama over its annual budget, which threatens to topple yet another leader.
